editorial:
Cheung Tin Chi is trying to leave his fighting days behind and raise his young son in Hong Kong, working as a waiter at a bar that serves expats. But the city has other plans. When a run-in with a powerful triad boss and a corrupt foreign businessman pulls him back into the action, Tin Chi has to decide whether to stay quiet or stand up for what's right. The movie has a fun, old-school martial arts feel with a modern crime story mixed in. You get flashy fights, colorful characters, and a father-son bond that gives the whole thing heart.

The action scenes are the real star here, with creative choreography and plenty of high-flying kicks. Max Zhang is great as Tin Chi, and Michelle Yeoh and Dave Bautista add serious star power. The story can feel a bit crowded at times, and some side plots don't get enough room to breathe. Still, if you love martial arts movies with strong fight scenes and a clear good-versus-evil story, this one delivers. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture.
endingExplained: In the final act, Tin Chi faces off against the corrupt foreign businessman Owen Davidson and the triad leader Tso Sai Kit. After a brutal showdown, Tin Chi defeats Davidson in a rooftop fight and exposes the criminal network. Tso Sai Kit is arrested, and Tin Chi walks away with his son, choosing peace over violence. The movie ends with Tin Chi reopening his martial arts school, passing on his skills to a new generation while keeping his promise to protect his family.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves martial arts action and crime dramas.
